intro:
BATTLE OF SESENA - 29 OCT 1936

South of Madrid, Spain

Comrade, here is your order - Move west with your armored forces and occupy the towns of Esquivias and Illescas! Support this move with your air force. Your infantry occupied Sesena and defend the town against enemy attacks. Good luck!

ORDERS
After 8 turns control 3/2/1 VH for a BV/V/TV.

briliant.text:
BRILLIANT VICTORY

You have achieved all objectives comrade, the operation was a complete success. Great work!

victory.text:
VICTORY

You have achieved most objectives comrade, the operation was a success. Good work!

tactical.text:
TACTICAL VICTORY

You have achieved some objectives comrade, after all, the operation was not a complete failure.

lose.text:
DEFEAT

No, nothing Comrade Marshal, we lost all communications after that last counterattack. They are all dead or prisoners!

CAMPAIGN LOST!

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: This Story Mode follows one composite operational dossier across successive Soviet commands from Spain to Manchuria. Volkov, Sokolova, Antonov, and Orlov are fictional staff figures: they make the decisions audible without attributing invented words or impossible careers to real commanders.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The tank crews have painted over every marking, but the dust identifies them well enough. Spanish infantrymen watch the engines turn over and ask the interpreters whether armour can really decide the day before nightfall.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: This is our first live test of a force built around tanks, aircraft, and radio. We can drive hard for the western towns, or keep the arms close enough that a local success does not leave Seseña exposed. Which lesson do we intend to learn?

choices.text: Concentrate the tanks and aircraft on a fast thrust toward Illescas.
choices.hint: Gain prestige and formation experience from a bold armoured demonstration, but forgo the prepared refit of the balanced plan.

choices.text: Advance by bounds, keeping infantry and artillery tied to the armoured column.
choices.hint: Restore every core unit to at least eight strength, replenish fuel and ammunition, and gain deeper formation experience; forgo the prestige award attached to the faster plan.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: Then speed is the protection. The leading companies will bypass resistance that cannot threaten the road and leave marked targets for the aircraft.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Then no arm outruns the others. The tanks will take the towns, but every captured road must remain usable by the infantry and guns behind them.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Whatever happens here will be studied far from Spain. Make certain the report records more than the number of kilometres gained.

orders.situation: A small Soviet-supported armoured group is committed south of Madrid while Republican infantry holds Seseña.
orders.mission: Take Esquivias and Illescas, support the advance from the air, and keep the Seseña position from becoming isolated.

intro:

Lake Khasan, Far East of Soviet Union

The sneaky Japanese attacked and beaten our border troops on the Bezymyannaya and Zaozyornaya hills. Attack the Japanese with superior power and recapture the territories we deserve!

ORDERS
After 9 turns control 7/6/5 VH for a BV/V/TV.

2x Infantry (+2)
1x Reconnaissance
1x Artillery (+1)

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The result at Seseña exceeded the operation's timetable. The staff arrives with confidence—and with expectations that the next battle will be just as clean.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov

dialogue.text: The force came through Seseña by the narrowest acceptable margin. Headquarters calls the objective achieved; the replacement lists describe how little room remains.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Seseña ended in failure, but the campaign has not released this command. The surviving formations report for another operation before the previous losses have been fully counted.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The previous decision—armoured spearhead—is now part of the staff's working method. Its advantage is visible, but so is the capability we chose not to prepare.

dialogue.text: The core reports no formation destroyed in the last operation. That continuity is now a real advantage: crews know one another, and orders move faster than replacements.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The last operation cost more than two core formations. New crews have filled spaces on the strength return, but not the habits and trust that vanished with them.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: Survey stakes disappear into the mud as quickly as the engineers plant them. From the observation post the hills look close; every approach between here and their slopes is wet, exposed, and already registered by enemy guns.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The border must be restored, but a map line does not tell us how to reach it. We can mass everything against the heights, or spend precious hours preparing lanes through the marsh and coordinating the batteries.

choices.text: Mass the striking force and keep pressure on both heights without pause.
choices.hint: Gain prestige and formation experience through relentless pressure, but forgo the full ammunition and recovery programme.

choices.text: Let engineers mark firm approaches and artillery register before the infantry moves.
choices.hint: Restore every core unit to at least eight strength, replenish fuel and ammunition, and gain deeper formation experience; forgo the prestige award attached to the faster plan.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The attack will not stop to reorganise on the lower slopes. Reserves follow the first success before the defenders can shift between the hills.

dialogue.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
dialogue.text: The first wave waits for marked lanes and observed fire. We lose surprise in minutes, but not battalions in unmarked marsh.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The heights are the visible objective. The harder task is proving that command and supply can reach them together.

orders.mission: Retake the occupied heights while preserving enough combat power to hold them after the assault.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov

Southeast of Grodno, East Poland

Move your units across the city of Grodno to the Lithuanian border. Occupy the city and vicinity and break any resistance!

Raate-Suomussalmi Road, Eastern Finland

Our comrades from the 163rd division in Suomussalmi are cut off and need help. Break through the enemy encirclement and restore the supply route!

a. Reach the Exit Point (Road to Suomussalmi) with at least 5 of your ground units.
b. Prevent that the enemy destroy more than 4 of your units.

NOTES
a. The Finns will try to surprise you. Be aware!
b. Attention - winter conditions! If possible, equip your troops with tracked movement. Check if you can switch between wheeled and tracked movement for free.

West of Minsk, Belarus

The treacherous Germans have launched a general attack on our homeland. The western front has collapsed and most of our troops are threatened to be encircled west of Minsk. Escape before the pocket closes! Make your way through the mess to the east!

Reach the Exit Points in time with at least 10 of your ground units before the enemy capture all VH!

c. Save your core units! Reach the Exit Points as soon as possible - don't get into a fight you can't win. There should also be useful attachments to make your units faster!

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The result at Vienna exceeded the operation's timetable. The staff arrives with confidence—and with expectations that the next battle will be just as clean.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Vienna was secured, though the formations carry its cost into the new operation. The result gives us options, not immunity from another mistake.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The force came through Vienna by the narrowest acceptable margin. Headquarters calls the objective achieved; the replacement lists describe how little room remains.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: Vienna ended in failure, but the campaign has not released this command. The surviving formations report for another operation before the previous losses have been fully counted.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The previous decision—cut the retreat—is now part of the staff's working method. Its advantage is visible, but so is the capability we chose not to prepare.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The previous decision—secure the road—carried the force here in better order. It also gave the enemy time or ground that cannot be reclaimed by paperwork.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The core reports no formation destroyed in the last operation. That continuity is now a real advantage: crews know one another, and orders move faster than replacements.

dialogue.speaker: Pavel Antonov
dialogue.text: The last operation cost more than two core formations. New crews have filled spaces on the strength return, but not the habits and trust that vanished with them.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: European place names have been erased from the board and replaced by rivers, railways, and distances most of the staff last studied before 1941. Veteran formations recognise the procedure; none recognises the country ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: We can force the crossings on the first timetable and pursue before the defence understands the scale of the attack, or build secure bridgeheads that can carry the whole army into the interior.

choices.text: Force the crossings at once and send mobile columns west before resistance can organise.
choices.hint: Gain prestige and experience for a final rapid operation, but forgo the complete replenishment of the secure bridgeheads.

choices.text: Secure every crossing with engineers, artillery, and supply before releasing the pursuit.
choices.hint: Restore every core unit to at least eight strength, replenish fuel and ammunition, and gain deeper formation experience; forgo the prestige award attached to the faster plan.

dialogue.speaker: Anna Sokolova
dialogue.text: The first columns carry fuel and bridging stores ahead of everything else. Once across, they do not wait for a European-style front to form around them.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: The bridgeheads are the operation's foundation. The pursuit begins when roads, guns, and ambulances can cross the same river as the tanks.

dialogue.speaker: Sergei Volkov
dialogue.text: From Madrid to Khabarovsk, the recurring question has never been speed or strength alone. It has been whether command can turn either one into an operation that survives its first success.

orders.situation: Three months after victory in Europe, the Soviet Union has entered the war against Japan. Forces near Khabarovsk must cross the border rivers and break into Manchuria.
orders.mission: Overcome the river defences, seize every objective, and open the route west before distance and terrain slow the offensive.
secondaryObjectives: Preserve the persistent core and its commanders for the next operation

epilogues.speaker: Anna Sokolova
epilogues.text: The river line broke before a stable front could form. The final pages of the dossier record distance, surrendered garrisons, and an army still moving when Japan's capitulation made further objectives unnecessary.

epilogues.speaker: Pavel Antonov
epilogues.text: The bridgeheads carried guns, fuel, ambulances, and then the pursuing columns. The final pages of the dossier record an operation that did not outrun its own support before Japan's capitulation ended the campaign.

epilogues.speaker: Sergei Volkov
epilogues.text: The attempt to race beyond the rivers spent its momentum before it could become an operation. The war ended elsewhere, leaving this command to account for a final objective it did not secure.

epilogues.speaker: Sergei Volkov
epilogues.text: The crossings were organised, but the advance never broke the border defence in time. The war ended elsewhere, and the dossier closes on a force preserved without completing its last mission.
